title: Ultrasound radiomics models diagnose cervical lymph node metastasis in lung cancer
summary: Logistic regression and random forest models on ultrasound radiomic and semantic features were developed for 313 NSCLC patients from three institutes, 276 (88.18%) with cervical lymph node metastasis. The semantic-radiomics combined random forest model had the highest hold-out AUC of 0.901 (95% CI 0.886-0.968), and combined models outperformed semantic-only and radiomics-only models. The study is retrospective and the high metastasis prevalence limits interpretation.
ai_technology: Random forest and logistic regression models on ultrasound radiomic and semantic features
organization: West China Hospital, Sichuan University; Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College; North Sichuan Medical College

evidence.tested: Fivefold cross-validation and an external hold-out test across institutes.
evidence.unknown: Prospective performance; behavior at lower metastasis prevalence; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Classifies cervical lymph nodes as metastatic from ultrasound-derived features.
